identity.name: The New York Times
identity.description: An American newspaper of record with global reporting, investigations, opinion and a large digital subscription business.

ownership.ownershipNotes: Publicly traded company controlled through a dual-class share structure by the Ochs-Sulzberger family, which has chaired the company since 1896.

editorialOrientation.evidence: Separate news and opinion operations with published standards; editorially independent of government, though owned by a controlling family.
editorialOrientation.source: Ownership and self-description via Official about page; secondary references; feed-level sample

politicalLeaning.evidence: MBFC rates Left-Center and High factual reporting; news reporting is professionally sourced while opinion and selection lean progressive.

economicPerspective.evidence: Economic coverage ranges from market-friendly to social-democratic; no single owner-directed economic line.

internationalAlignment.evidence: Frames global events through a US/liberal-internationalist lens, with substantial critical reporting on US policy.
internationalAlignment.source: Ownership, editorial positioning and regional coverage sample

reliability.evidence: MBFC rates factual reporting High and credibility High; long-established corrections, investigations and named sourcing.

externalRatings.notes: MBFC: Left-Center; factual reporting High; credibility High (retrieved 2026-10-25).

intelligence.knownPerspective: US newspaper-of-record voice. Sets agenda through investigative and explanatory reporting, generally within a liberal-internationalist framework, with strong domestic-politics and culture coverage.

selectionRationale: A global agenda-setter with investigative depth; already active and valuable for US and international coverage.

research.researchNotes: Existing production mapping retained. RSS provides headlines and summaries, not full paywalled articles. Research is feed-level only; full article sampling and peer review remain outstanding.
